findings.text: The `self` pattern catches more than it should. Only five of its ten hits are a speaker calling himself poor: 1Sa 18:23, Psa 40:17, Psa 70:5, Psa 86:1 and Psa 109:22. The other five are Luk 4:18, Isa 61:1, Luk 19:8, Job 29:16 and Job 30:25. The markers are a working aid only: they point to verses to read and decide nothing.

Means, set against the rich: "A rich man's wealth is his strong city; the poverty of the poor is their ruin" (Pro 10:15); "The rich rules over the poor" (Pro 22:7); "The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less" (Exo 30:15); "one of your brothers should become poor … you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand" (Deu 15:7).

Poor where the verse separates what is said or seen from what is so: "One pretends to be rich, yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth" (Pro 13:7); "you say, 'I am rich … I need nothing,' not realizing that you are … poor" (Rev 3:17); "as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything" (2Co 6:10); "poor in the world to be rich in faith" (Jam 2:5); "though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor" (2Co 8:9).

Poor joined to the spirit or heart: "Blessed are the poor in spirit" (Mat 5:3); "better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor" (Pro 16:19); "I am poor and needy, and my heart is stricken within me" (Psa 109:22).

Poor or needy said by the speaker as the ground of a plea: "answer me, for I am poor and needy" (Psa 86:1); "I am poor and needy; hasten to me, O God!" (Psa 70:5); "As for me, I am poor and needy, but the Lord takes thought for me" (Psa 40:17).
Poor said of one's own standing: "since I am a poor man and have no reputation" (1Sa 18:23).
The poor appealing to others: "The poor use entreaties, but the rich answer roughly" (Pro 18:23); "you hear the desire of the afflicted" (Psa 10:17); "he cry to the Lord against you" (Deu 15:9).

Note for reading. In Psa 40:17, 70:5, 86:1 and 109:22, "poor" in "poor and needy" is H6041 ʿānî, which is tagged M24, and "needy" is H0034 (M09). This was checked in `verse_lexical`. These verses therefore sit on both sides of the M09 / M24 line.

Seeing is often named. These are quoted, not read: "Blessed is the one who considers the poor!" (Psa 41:1); "if I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing" (Job 31:19); "If you see in a province the oppression of the poor" (Ecc 5:8); "Whoever has a bountiful eye … shares his bread with the poor" (Pro 22:9); "he who hides his eyes will get many a curse" (Pro 28:27); "your eye look grudgingly on your poor brother" (Deu 15:9); "His eyes stealthily watch for the helpless" (Psa 10:8).

What the sight moves in a person, as the verses name it (G-person): "Was not my soul grieved for the needy?" (Job 30:25); "He has pity on the weak and the needy" (Psa 72:13, the king); "you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand" (Deu 15:7); "an unworthy thought in your heart" (Deu 15:9); "Whoever mocks the poor … he who is glad at calamity" (Pro 17:5); "The poor is disliked even by his neighbor" (Pro 14:20); "All a poor man's brothers hate him" (Pro 19:7); "the poor man's wisdom is despised" (Ecc 9:16); "These are only the poor; they have no sense" (Jer 5:4); "no one remembered that poor man" (Ecc 9:15); "the very thing I was eager to do" (Gal 2:10); "pleased to make some contribution for the poor" (Rom 15:26); "not because he cared about the poor" (Joh 12:6); "the master of the house became angry and said … bring in the poor" (Luk 14:21).

What the sight moves in God (G-God): "Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, I will now arise," says the Lord (Psa 12:5); "But you do see … to you the helpless commits himself" (Psa 10:14); "he does not forget the cry of the afflicted" (Psa 9:12); "he regards the prayer of the destitute" (Psa 102:17); "I the Lord will answer them" (Isa 41:17); "He raises the poor from the dust" (Psa 113:7; 1Sa 2:8).

Where a verse joins the two sides: "Whoever oppresses a poor man insults his Maker, but he who is generous to the needy honors him" (Pro 14:31); "Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker" (Pro 17:5); "Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the Lord" (Pro 19:17); "He judged the cause of the poor and needy … Is not this to know me? declares the Lord" (Jer 22:16); "The rich and the poor meet together; the Lord is the Maker of them all" (Pro 22:2); "Did not he who made me in the womb make him?" (Job 31:15).

Two notes for reading: The same verses often set the poor beside the widow, the fatherless and the sojourner, for example Job 31:16, Deu 24:14, Isa 10:2, Psa 10:14 and Psa 82:3. Those words are not M09 and are not pulled; Of the 27 verses with no other M-code, that reading's groups B (Bethany) and D (the ruler, Zacchaeus) and most of E fall in G-person. The poor widow (its group C) and Lazarus at the gate (Luk 16:20) are B proper: the verse puts the poor person first.

Surface: humble (9), afflicted (5), poor (4), meek (4). This one word is rendered on both sides of the cluster's definition. Examples: "the meek" (Num 12:3 of Moses; Psa 37:11); "the humble" (Pro 3:34; Psa 25:9); "the afflicted" (Psa 9:12; 10:12); "the poor" (Isa 61:1; Pro 16:19).
D. H1793A dakkāʾ "contrite": Isa 57:15 ("contrite and lowly spirit") and Psa 34:18 ("crushed in spirit"). Both are cited in the narrative.
E. G5292 hypotagē "submission": 2Co 9:13, Gal 2:5, 1Ti 2:11, 1Ti 3:4.
F. G3635 okneō "to delay": Act 9:38 ("do not delay"). It came in by old-system migration. Its gloss has no bearing on humility.
In Isa 66:2, "humble" is H6041 ʿānî (M24) and "contrite" is H5223 (M73). The verse carries no M09 word at all. Psa 51:17 is the same: its broken and contrite words are in M24 and M10.

This is where the change-of-character reading (#1919) would start. No reading has been done: H3665 kānaʿ: "humbled himself" (kings in 2Ch, 1Ki 21:29, 2Ki 22:19) versus "subdued" (nations in Judg, 1Sa 7:13, 2Sa 8:1, 1Ch 18:1, Psa 81:14). It is the same verb for humbling oneself before God and for being brought low by another; H8217 šāphāl: "lowly" (Isa 57:15; Psa 138:6; Pro 29:23) versus "deeper than the skin" (Lev 13 and 14, leprosy, 4 verses) versus "low" of a vine and a kingdom (Eze 17; 29:14–15); G5012 tapeinophrosynē: "humility" (Phili 2:3; Col 3:12; Eph 4:2; 1Pe 5:5; Act 20:19) versus "asceticism" (Col 2:18, 23); H6035 ʿānāw: humble / afflicted / poor / meek, as in §3C; H1800 dal: poor / weak / "haggard" (2Sa 13:4, Amnon); G4434 ptōchos: poor / "worthless" (Gal 4:9, the elementary principles).

Points that follow from the scan, with no reading done: ʿānî (H6041) is the partner of ʿānāw and of "poor and needy". It shares 32 verses with M09. This accounts for much of M24's place as M09's largest co-occurring cluster; "Humility" as a noun in the OT (Pro 15:33; 18:12; 22:4, H6038) sits in M05, not M09; "Meek" and "gentle" in the NT (Mat 5:5; 11:29; Gal 5:23) sit in M05; H8213 šāphēl, "to bring low", sits in M53. Its 29 verses include 1Sa 2:7, Psa 18:27, Pro 29:23, Isa 2:9–17 and Eze 21:26.

M08 Pride & Arrogance (23 verses) holds the paired sayings, for example: Jam 4:6, 1Pe 5:5 and Pro 3:34 ("opposes the proud, gives grace to the humble"); Pro 29:23 and Pro 11:2; Psa 138:6, Job 5:11 and Job 22:29; Eze 17:24 and Eze 21:26; Dan 4:37.

What earlier strands already hold for M09: M18 (23 shared verses), OT-97 item 17 (`cluster:M09`). Three verses are marked forward to M09: Job 31:16 and Rom 15:26 (group B triage v2) and Mar 14:7 (group C triage v2). The others were decided in the M18 strand. For example, Pro 22:9 was read and Mat 19:21 was carried in 10.6; M02 (6 shared verses), OT-103 item 44 (`cluster:M09`): Luk 14:21, 2Ch 12:7, 2Ch 12:12, 2Ch 32:26, Zep 2:3 and Psa 10:14. In the 2Ch verses, God's wrath turns when the king humbles himself; M72 (33 shared verses). The group D forward list (`m72-group-D-forward-v2-20261012.csv`) marks 9 hand verses forward to M09: 2Ch 12:7, Jer 20:13, Psa 82:4, Neh 9:24, 1Sa 7:13, 2Sa 8:1, 1Ch 18:1, Job 5:15 and Psa 106:42. Most of them are H3665 "subdued" or "the needy". Neh 9:24 was already read and woven in M18 group C; M47 (34 shared verses). Under the #1979 closure, each strand checks its M47 verses for dropped placements, by word and not by citation (OT-09). The earlier M47 assessment lists M09 under "D. Moral condition" (`M47-other-cluster-cooccurrence-assessment-v1-20260927.md`); M25 (14 shared verses). The life-death overview gives these pairings: to live + low (Isa 57:15), to die + needy (Isa 14:30, Psa 109:16), to die + poor (Luk 16:22); Open threads matched (`Escalation.ps1 -Action Match -Cluster M09 -Strong <26>`): only OT-97 (item 17) and OT-103 (item 44). No thread names an M09 Strong's or verse directly.

Verses with no other M-code (27). Unlike the M64 choose verses that were parked (OT-93), these include verses central to the cluster: Num 12:3 (Moses very meek); Mat 23:12, Luk 14:11 and Jam 4:10 (humble yourself and be exalted); Luk 1:52 ("exalted those of humble estate"); 2Sa 6:22 (David "abased in my own eyes"); the widow's offering (Mar 12:42; Luk 21:3).

Group A, the humbling words (12 Strong's, 86 verses), with D (contrite, 2 verses). These words are closest to the inner act the definition names: humbling oneself, a lowly spirit, humility: Group B, poor and needy, now split; G, the poor as seen by another (127 verses): what the sight moves in a person (93) and in God (34); B proper, the poor person's own state, standing and voice (48 verses). This is where the researcher's dimensions are tested; The poverty word is not a qualifier by default (rule 73, per occurrence); H6035 ʿānāw (21 verses), which spans A and B, together with its partner H6041 ʿānî (M24, 32 shared verses); The words outside M09. None is re-tagged (#1970). Whether any is read with this strand is for you to say.
